My daughter-in-law brought our family dog to Dr. Vasquez because the dog was suffering from an ear infection. We trusted Dr. Vasquez to properly diagnose and treat the condition. She recommended two surgeries, which were agreed to at a total cost of $2,600.
What happened afterward was devastating. Despite seeking veterinary care and trusting the doctor’s recommendations, my grandson’s emotional support animal tragically died.
This was not just a pet to our family. This dog was my grandson’s emotional support animal and an important part of his life. Losing him has caused our family tremendous emotional pain.
We trusted Dr. Vasquez with the care and safety of a beloved member of our family, and we are deeply disappointed and heartbroken by the outcome. We believe the circumstances surrounding the treatment and the decisions that were made deserve a thorough explanation. We are seeking answers regarding what happened, why the surgeries were recommended, and whether everything possible was done to prevent this tragic outcome.

Stay away from animal medical center and spa on Miller and 157 if you want to keep your pet alive.

Story below for reference:

The Last Night With Dominoe 8/28/26😞 🐶

Just to add: dominoe was amazingly healthy. No preliminary problems whatsoever. We brought him to the vet for an ear infection 😞

Just trying to get some awareness out there while we grieve our loss.

Last night started like any other night. We took our sweet Dominoe to a new veterinarian because he had an ear infection. We thought we were doing what any loving family would do—getting him the care he needed and making sure he was okay.

The bill came to an unbelievable $2,600 for both ears hematoma repair and neutering (upsold on this). We paid it because, to us, Dominoe was worth everything. We also made the decision to have him neutered while he was there. We trusted that when we brought him home, he would be safe.

(For the record he has had this condition maybe twice before, treated at a different hospital for not even 1/4 of the price.) the vet that receive him at the ER when we showed up with him, said he’d never seen a dog die from such routine procedures at such a young age. Also advised even at his emergency clinic that same bill would have been max 1K.

And then we brought our boy home.

He was home with his family. We thought we had him back.

Only about an hour later, we went to bring Dominoe upstairs with us so he could sleep in our room, just like he belonged.

But when we found him, he was dead and not breathing.

He was gone.

There are no words for what it feels like to lose someone you were just holding onto an hour before. One minute, you are thinking about taking care of your dog, getting him comfortable, and spending the night together. The next, you are standing there in complete disbelief, wondering how this could possibly be real.

We keep replaying everything in our heads.

We keep asking why.

We keep wishing we could go back just a few hours and somehow change what happened.

Dominoe wasn’t “just a dog.” He was family. He was part of our home, our routines, our hearts, and our lives. His little presence filled spaces that now feel painfully empty.

Our family is absolutely wrecked.

We didn’t get a chance to say goodbye. We didn’t know that when we brought him home last night, it would be the last time we’d ever see our sweet boy alive.

We thought we were taking Dominoe to the vet to help him.

We never imagined we would bring him home for the last time.

Tonight, our house feels different. There is an emptiness that shouldn’t be here. We keep expecting to hear him, see him, or have him walk into the room like he always did.

Dominoe deserved more time.

He deserved to grow old surrounded by the people who loved him.

And we deserved more time with him.

We will never understand why our last night together became our goodbye.

But one thing we know for certain is that Dominoe was deeply loved. Every dollar we spent, every worry we had, every decision we made was because we loved him and wanted him to be okay.

Our hearts are shattered.

Run free, sweet Dominoe. ❤️🐾

You were loved more than you could ever have known, and you will never, ever be forgotten.

Until we meet again, our sweet boy.

Please do not take your dogs or animals to Animal Medical Center and Spa

We will make sure everyone in the state of Florida knows about this vet and what happened to our dog.

My experience at the clinic:

I wanted to leave my review today because I know many people, like me, look for references before taking their pets to a place.

Regarding the staff in general, and especially Dr. Carmen, I can say that everything has been fine. She is excellent at her job and has treated my dogs with dedication and professionalism. That's why I went several times, on my brother's recommendation and because it's close to home.

However, my experience at reception with Mrs. Rosa has been the complete opposite. From the beginning, her attitude has been unfriendly. On one occasion, she hung up the phone while I was trying to explain that I should bring my dog ​​back 10 days after the treatment, not before, as per medical advice, to see if her persistent cough had cleared up.

Today, Monday, when I arrived, I greeted her with a "good morning" and avoided starting a conversation. When I received my bill, as is normal, I asked what procedure had been performed and why that amount. In the past, they've overcharged me, but they've always credited my account without issue.

This time, her reaction was very inappropriate: she told me I'm always dissatisfied and that "no one at the vet clinic likes my attitude."

I want to clarify that my only problem has been with her. I've always been respectful to the team, and I've never had any issues with the doctor or the rest of the staff. Ms. Rosa ended up telling me she was inviting me to stop coming, because she "will always be here."

So, I'll stop coming. Thank you.

I’m attaching the review my daughter posted and Animal Medical Center and Spa’s response. I posted in Yelp as well. My daughter’s review covers the issue but I want to add something. In the clinic’s response, they practically blame us for Jackie’s death. It’s true that we refused to let her stay at the clinic for the weekend and the reason is that they don’t have personnel for constant supervision on weekends. We didn’t want her to be alone in a cage with IVs that were not going to alleviate the situation. When my granddaughter first arrived in the clinic with Jackie, she was put in a cage to wait for the doctor to examine her. My granddaughter said she was there and she could hold her until she was called. Jackie had had another diarrhea in the brief moments she was in the cage and they gave her back without even bothering to clean her up. I wonder what would have happened if we had left her there for two nights. Yes, we took her home but we left with her medications and her special food and the directions the doctor gave us. We didn’t take her home to “euthanize her.” The doctor said she wanted to see Jackie on Monday, that made us think that there was hope. The bill for the visit was over $1,116, and that was without the ultrasound and the boarding. We never blamed the clinic or the doctor for Jackie’s death, we knew the end was near, she was 16 and a half years old. What upset us was the false hope and the recommendations for boarding, IVs, and tests that were not going to save her. If you read other reviews here, you’ll see other complaints about the clinic always being overbooked and the difference between estimates and final cost. We kept taking Jackie to your clinic because 16 years ago there were not major problems, the prices were decent, and the front desk people acted like they actually cared, they listened to us. The doctors were also outstanding, mainly Dr. Oñate who was the one who most frequently took care of Jackie. I think it’s very cruel that you blame us for Jackie’s passing. Good luck in the future and please, address negative comments with the desire of coming back to be the great clinic you once were.

I’ve been dealing with ongoing issues with Rosa, the owner, for a while now. The biggest problem is the lack of transparency around pricing. We’re often given a the price and told what will be done to our pets, but when we show up, there are additional charges added without warning. Rosa acts like we should have known about these extra costs, even though she never clearly communicated them upfront. On top of that, if you do get an explanation, it’s not the full story — she’ll tell you one price and then try to charge more. In one case, my sister had to contact her bank for a refund because she wasn’t told the correct price in advance and after Rosa was told no she won't pay for it bc she wasn't told that price Rosa was trying to charge her Rosa then went behind my sisters back and charged her card with the numbers she got off a recording that was made on one phone call with the vet office.

It’s clear that for Rosa, misleading customers has become second nature. When I volunteered there as a vet assistant student from ferg, I saw this happen regularly. The vet is great, but Rosa has no clue how to run a business, and her customer service skills are non-existent. She even tries to deny adding extra services to bills when we’ve repeatedly asked her receptionists to remove services we didn’t authorize. We've been stuck paying for things we never asked for a couple times because our dogs didnt need them

The final straw was what happened to my sister. Now, they won’t even release our dogs' records so we can take them to a different vet. I strongly advise against going here. If you do, at least call ahead so you don’t have to deal with Rosa. I honestly don’t understand how someone can run a business and be so clueless about their own pricing or how to treat customers. Rosa needs to do better.
